catalog_quote: [sec. 2.5, pp. 12-13] Tiefo-D has some atonal morphemes that really should be transcribed without tonal diacritics in their lexical form to distinguish them from M-toned forms. Tiefo-N has no atonal morphemes. ... Tiefo-N too has three tone levels, but they pattern differently. Whereas W98 reports many M-toned nouns for Tiefo-D, Tiefo-N has none (except in HM-toned stems). ... As this suggests, M-tone is not regular for monosyllabic nouns in Tiefo-N. For nouns, it occurs only as part of HM sequences. On the other hand, grammatical particles and verb forms may be M-toned. Contoured tones within a syllable in Tiefo-N are limited to two falling contours (<HL> and <HM>), one rising contour <LH>, and (rarely) a bell-shaped contour <LHL>. [sec. 2.7, p. 18] There are three tone levels: H, M, and L. [sec. 2.7.1, p. 18] Slashes /…/ enclose lexical tone melodies. Monosyllabic Tiefo-N nouns may be…

new_statements.rule_in_words: Tiefo-N is described as a three-level tone language (H, M, L, with lexical tone melodies on nouns, tonal ablaut on verbs and tone sandhi); the grammar has no section on and makes no claim about word stress or accent. The single occurrence of 'stress' refers to a phonetic pulse inside intonationally prolonged plural vowels, not to lexical or fixed word stress.
new_statements.exceptions: None; no stress system is posited. (For the sister language Tiefo-D, Heath & Ouattara 2021:79 explicitly state 'There is no evidence in favor of an accentual interpretation of tones' and p.75 'no stress or accent shifts due to addition of a morpheme', but no equivalent sentence exists in the Tiefo-N grammar.)
new_statements.domain_note: Tone described at word (lexical melody) and phrase (sandhi) level; no word-stress domain discussed. Data are elicited citation forms and phrases from the last two fluent speakers; no running texts exist for Tiefo-N.
new_statements.identity_note: Heath, Ouattara & Hantgan 2017 describe Tiefo-N as spoken by the last two fluent speakers in Nyafogo (Gnanfogo) village; the closely related Numudara (Noumoudara) variety was already extinct. This is exactly Glottolog's tief1244 'Tiefo-Nyafogo-Numudara'. The sister language Tiefo-D of Daramandugu (tief1242) is a distinct language covered by Heath & Ouattara 2021 (already in the catalog); Winkelmann 1998, named by the earlier scan, is a Tiefo-D grammar with only lexical Tiefo-N comparisons, not a Tiefo-N description.

sources.note: Phonology ch.2 (pp.8-23): sec. 2.5 'Tones: Inventory and transcription' (pp.12-13) and 2.7 'Tonology' (pp.18-23) give three tone levels H/M/L, lexical noun melodies, contour tones, tone sandhi; 'Tiefo-N has no atonal morphemes'. No section or sentence on word stress/accent anywhere (grep of full text: 'stress' occurs only once, p.30 sec. 3.1.2, 'a stress-like pulse in the middle of the long vowel' in prolonged plural vowels; 'accent' never). Silent on stress; language treated as purely tonal.

sources.citation: Heath, Jeffrey & Aminata Ouattara. 2021. A Grammar of Tiefo-D of Daramandugu. Language Description Heritage Library / Zenodo 10.5281/zenodo.4715103. xxii+759 pp. [Tiefo-D, tief1242]
sources.note: Describes the sister language Tiefo-D, not Tiefo-N; checked only its sections 1.2 and 1.5 for the state of Tiefo-N scholarship: confirms the 2017 short grammar is the only Tiefo-N grammar, that no Tiefo-N texts exist, and that 'Ouattara defended her master's thesis on Tiefo-N in 2019'. Its own prosody statements (3 tone levels, 'no evidence in favor of an accentual interpretation of tones') apply to Tiefo-D.

sources.note: Brief phonology overview only; p.120: 'Tiefo-N and Tiefo-D also have the same three tone levels. High tones are marked by an acute accent [á], low tones by a grave accent [à]. Mid tones are written either without an accent (Winkelmann 1998) or more explicitly with a macron [ā].' Nothing on stress.
